name: PA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+40 partisan lean of the Philadelphia district
Democrat Chris Rabb heavily outraises and outspends independent Dennis Mahoney
Open seat after Dwight Evans' retirement
model.rationale: The district's D+40 lean makes a Democratic hold overwhelming, and Rabb's roughly $1.3 million raised plus $1.6 million in outside support dwarfs Mahoney's $10,800 campaign. Markets price a Democratic win near certainty, so the baseline margin stands.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or a strong independent consolidation of moderate voters could narrow the margin, though not plausibly the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dwight Evans (D) is not on the ballot.
Dennis Mahoney is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
This deep-blue Philadelphia seat, rated D+40, is open after Dwight Evans' retirement. State Representative Chris Rabb is the Democratic nominee and enters the general election with a commanding financial edge: about $1.3 million raised and $1.6 million in outside support, against roughly $10,800 for independent Dennis Mahoney. No expert raters cover the race and no general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and spending.

Prediction markets put the Democratic side near 96 percent, consistent with the district's overwhelming partisan lean. The forecast expects Rabb to win by a wide, roughly thirty-point margin, with the seat firmly in the Safe D column.
